body.x: This vacancy announcement pertains to law enforcement and/or governmental officials within INTERPOL's member countries only.
Please read the Conditions of Secondment in force at INTERPOL (shared via the NCB) including the maximum duration of secondment.

Please be aware that your home Administration/Agency/Service/Government will be responsible for all of your salary/remuneration, social insurance, pension contributions, welfare benefits, family allowances, benefits during your assignment at INTERPOL as well as travel, removal expenses related to your arrival at and departure from INTERPOL, and any other related costs depending on your circumstances. It is requested that you obtain in writing, confirmation from your home Administration/Agency/Service/Government that it agrees with these CONDITIONS OF SECONDMENT. This confirmation letter should be forwarded to us THROUGH THE NCB.

INTERPOL is the world’s largest international police organization, with 196 member states. Created in 1923, it facilitates cross-border police co-operation, and supports and assists all organizations, authorities, and services whose mission is to prevent or combat international crime. INTERPOL is now looking for a qualified candidate as a SECONDMENT - Assistant Director Internal Innovation within the Innovation Centre which is part of the Exec. Dir. Capacity Building Innovation.
Job title: SECONDMENT - Assistant Director Internal Innovation

INTERPOL actively encourages applications from women and nationals of member countries that are currently unrepresented among our staff (please click on this link to access the list of countries). Candidates from these countries are particularly encouraged to apply.
INTERPOL’s recruitment process is merit-based hence all hiring decisions are made considering the applicant’s qualifications and the needs of the Organization.
INCLUDING GOALS AND OBJECTIVES OF THE POST

Within the Executive Directorate of Capacity Building and Innovation (EDCI), the Innovation Centre (IC) aims to support law enforcement agencies in understanding the rapid changes affecting policing. The Directorate facilitates knowledge exchange on how technologies impact law enforcement.

The objective is to serve as a transversal enabler for INTERPOL and its member countries, facilitating the sharing of law enforcement innovations, the identification of critical challenges, and the development of effective solutions with partners. In coordination with relevant internal directorates, the IC will support organization-wide innovation initiatives, particularly AI initiatives by contributing to the experimentation, prototyping, evaluation, and secure development of new capabilities. This includes providing a structured environment and framework for testing and validating use cases, while ensuring strict alignment with the Responsible Use of AI framework.
These efforts will be underpinned by an innovation platform that integrates the expertise of police, public and private partners, and academia.

Reporting to the Director of the Innovation Centre, the post holder will lead the Sub-Directorate in identifying the multifaceted needs and operational constraints of INTERPOL and its member countries to guide global innovation efforts for law enforcement. This strategic role entails monitoring the implementation of innovation initiatives across the Organization and fostering a culture of innovation for efficiency and effectiveness to help INTERPOL officials to find more impactful ways of working.
The post holder will be expected to work collaboratively with colleagues within the IC and across various INTERPOL units as well as with external partners.
Lead the co-development and implementation of innovative solutions, delivering tangible and practical results.
Oversee the management of Sub-Directorate staff and budget, ensuring effective resource allocation and utilization.
Identify and define innovation opportunities that address the operational needs of the internal units and the global law enforcement community, informing strategic priorities and initiatives.
Foster and maintain the Global Innovation Network and strategic partnerships with key stakeholders, promoting a collaborative and cooperative working environment.
DUTY 2: Facilitation of the CO-DEVELOPMENT of solutions

Facilitate the global law enforcement community's efforts to address emerging policing challenges, by creating an environment for testing and refining potential solutions through pilot trials and testbeds.

Guild efforts to co-develop and maintain a comprehensive understanding of new technologies and solutions through rigorous research and close engagement with relevant stakeholders, both within and outside the global policing community.
Lead the coordination of the co-development of innovative research methodologies and tools, utilizing open-source intelligence and partnership contributions to drive progress and innovation.
DUTY 3: ASSITANCE in Management of Directorate
Define and implement KPIs for Innovation and integrate them into the organizational performance-management system.

Conduct in-depth analysis of Sub-Directorate issues and develop independent solutions, providing recommendations for projects, activities, and missions that align with the directorate's overall objectives and activities.
Prepare accurate and timely reports on actions taken, sharing them with relevant teams and officers across the directorate to facilitate information sharing and collaboration.

Represent the hierarchy in their absence, as required, at organizational and international conferences, meetings, and missions, liaising directly with senior officials, including Directors and Assistant Directors, and maintaining effective relationships.
Perform any other duty as required by the hierarchy.
At least five years’ University education, with a specialization, master's degree, or doctorate in a relevant field such as engineering, science, public policy, or law.
Advanced law enforcement training at a senior level is required.
Fluency in English is required (both in written and oral form).
Proficiency in a second official working language of the Organization (Arabic, French or Spanish) would be an additional asset.
A minimum of 10 years of policing experience, including at least 5 years in a management role with a proven track record of strategic decision-making and leadership.
In-depth knowledge of current and emerging computer and communications technologies, including their practical applications and implications for law enforcement.

Specialized experience in cybercrime, financial crime, counter-terrorism, or organized crime, with a strong understanding of the legal frameworks and international agreements governing transnational investigations.
Proven ability to independently plan and manage complex tasks, utilizing strong problem-solving and strategic thinking skills to achieve results with minimal supervision.

Demonstrated experience in developing strategic partnerships and outreach programs, with a proven ability to maintain relationships with governments, international organizations, and law enforcement agencies.
Proven experience of hosting meetings and conferences with international participants. A track record of leading and coordinating several international conferences would be a considerable asset.
Ability to articulate the link between organizational strategy and unit goals, utilizing proactive and strategic thinking to develop and implement plans that inspire and motivate staff.
A supportive leadership style focused on empowering staff through delegation, clear expectations, and autonomy, complemented by strong performance management, coaching, and inclusive teamwork.
Sound judgment and analytical skills to make informed, timely decisions, alongside effective budget management to ensure resources are used efficiently.
Excellent presentation and communication abilities, with a proven capacity to build trust and foster a positive, inclusive work environment.
Demonstrated ability to build professional partnerships with governments, international organizations, and academia while working effectively in a multicultural environment.
As part of our commitment to transparency throughout our recruitment process, INTERPOL's Staff Manual Regulation 11.4: Age-limit, which states that:

'Officials of the Organization shall not normally be retained in service beyond the age of 65 years. The Secretary General may, in exceptional cases and in the interests of the Organization, extend this age limit, in which case he shall inform the official concerned sufficiently in advance.'

Given this Regulation and in case candidates reach the age of 65 during the potential duration of the appointment, should they be selected for the position and the process proceed to appointment, the employment period may be affected by this regulatory limit and may therefore not extend for the full standard contract duration as published in the vacancy notice.
We are sharing this information to ensure transparency at this stage of the process.
This position is no longer open.
